newsitem.title: USA: Dow Jones index tumbles nearly 100 points.
newsitem.headline: Dow Jones index tumbles nearly 100 points.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks slumped for the second session in a row Thursday after a rollercoaster ride that saw the Dow fall, recover some losses and then drop sharply in late trading.

The Dow Jones industrial average ended down 98.81 points, or 1.54 percent, at 6,303.71 -- its biggest point loss since mid-July -- after giving back an early gain of 35 points. On Wednesday, it fell 71 points amid a host of bearish market rumours.
In the broader market, declining issues beat advances 1,616 to 877 on active volume of 492 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

"Investors were whipsawed. They were emboldened at the opening from two fabulous economic reports and then a wave of computer-driven sell orders took the market hostage. Trading is still nervous," said Philip Orlando, chief investment officer at Value Line Asset Management.
In a turbulent session, the NYSE imposed trading curbs twice as the 30-stock Dow index fell 50 points in mid-afternoon, recovered somewhat and then plummeted again in late trading.

"It has become clearly evident that we have already seen the high for the Dow for the short-term," said Richard Cripps, chief market strategist of Legg Mason Wood Walker. "There is a loss of momentum in the stock market."

The mood of investors soured last Friday after Chairman Alan Greenspan that rattled markets around the world with a warning about "irrational exuberance" in financial markets. The comment was viewed as a hint that the central bank might resort to higher interest rates to slow the markets' ascent.
On Friday, the Dow tumbled nearly 145 points before recovering to end 82 points lower.

Stocks steadied on Monday and Tuesday but the market was shaken anew Wednesday by speculation that Japanese investors might be losing their appetite for U.S. Treasury securities and amid jitters about corporate earnings.
"This nervousness is going to be with us the rest of the year -- nervousness because of the levels where we are," said Ned Collins, head of U.S. equity trading at Daiwa Securities America Inc.
"Portfolio managers are dying for this year to be over with -- to book some profits and look to next year, what with the rumours and bond movements," he said.

Among the Dow's biggest point losers were Disney, off 2 to 70-1/4, International Business Machines, down 4-1/2 to 151-5/8, 3M, off 2-7/8 to 80-1/4, Philip Morris, off 3-3/4 to 113-7/8, Merck, off 3 to 76-1/4, and United Technologies, off 2-1/8 to 63-1/2.
The bearishness was limited to the stock market, with bond holding steady after Wednesday shakeout.
The Treasury's 30-year bond edged up 2/32 point and its yield slipped to 6.62 percent from Wednesday's 6.63 percent and vs. 6.49 percent Tuesday.
Bonds warmly greeted November retail sales, which fell 0.4 percent, suggesting that the economy was slowing as expected and inflation was still not a threat.
In other economic news, the Consumer Price Index for November rose an expected 0.3 percent. That followed benign inflation data in Wednesday's November wholesale price report.
Bank stocks were hard-hit amid uncertainty over interest rates. Wells Fargo fell 3-1/2 to 264-1/2, Citicorp lost 2-3/8 to 98-5/8 and NationsBank fell 3-1/2 to 92-5/8.
BankAmerica fell 3-1/4 to 94. The company announced a major restructuring, including the elimination of 3,700 jobs worldwide.

Among other issues, Warner Lambert rose 7/8 to 76-1/4. Smith Barney upgraded the stock to buy after the Food and Drug Administration's advisory panel recommended approval Wednesday of its drug Rezulin to treat a form of diabetes.
Boston Technology surged 4-3/8 to 23-3/8 after agreeing to supply SBC Communications' Southwestern Bell with $60 million in hardware, software and services.
Tenneco slumped 6 to 45-1/2. The company completed the merger of Tenneco Energy with El Paso Natural Gas and the spin-off of its Newport News Shipbuilding unit.
The Nasdaq Composite index fell 10.79 to 1,298.33.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks was off 11.43 to 729.30. The American Stock Exchange index was off 4.81 to 579.11.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks fell 5.25 to 384.29. The average share was down 55 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 7,091.576 down 86.309 or 1.20 percent.
